label: FP
reason: Both alerts are False Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) reports sink at L61-L62, but resolved sink value is 'moresafe' (constant) due to list manipulation in doSomething shifting user input 'param'. Alert 2 (java/sql-injection) reports sink at L56, but resolved sink value is also 'moresafe' (constant). User input 'param' is added to list but removed/index-shifted such that it does not reach the sink expression.

evidence.note: SQL injection sink: queryForObject(sql). Resolved value of sql depends on bar which resolves to constant 'moresafe' via list manipulation (add/remove/get), excluding user param.
XSS sink: println(encodeForHTML(sql)). Resolved value of sql is constant 'moresafe', not user input, making encoding redundant and alert unfounded.
Control flow in doSomething: valuesList.remove(0) followed by get(1) retrieves 'moresafe' instead of user-provided param.
